title: Unit – 4 : Session – 10 : SLO – 2  |  Heaps
sections: A heap is a special TREE-BASED (complete binary tree) data structure.
Heaps are usually implemented as ARRAYS.
A MAX-heap has the largest element at the root.
A MIN-heap has the smallest element at the root.
A heap is a COMPLETE binary tree.
Heaps are used in PRIORITY queues.
In a max-heap, each parent is GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO its children.
In a min-heap, each parent is LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO its children.
Heap insertion is done at the LAST (next available leaf) position.
After insertion, we perform HEAPIFY-UP (up-heap / bubble-up) to maintain heap property.
Deletion is done from the ROOT of the heap.
After deletion, we perform HEAPIFY-DOWN (down-heap / reheapification).
Heaps can be efficiently stored using ARRAYS.
The time complexity for insertion and deletion in a heap is O(log n).
Heap sort is a sorting technique based on the HEAP data structure.
